text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.3% today as oil prices stabilized and geopolitical tensions in the Middle East eased slightly after weekend rhetoric. US crude is trading at $82.24 per barrel—down from recent highs but holding steady—while the broader international oil market at $91.80 per barrel suggests persistent demand. The company, as a major oil producer, benefits when crude prices remain above $80, since that improves margins on every barrel produced.

The stock's 2% decline over the past two weeks reflects the broader uncertainty around climate policy and energy demand: the failed fossil-fuel language at the U.N. climate summit created a brief relief for oil markets (since stricter climate commitments would have pressured demand), but it also highlighted ongoing political risk around the energy sector's long-term role.
